newsitem.title: USA: USTR in telecommunications deal with Korea.
newsitem.headline: USTR in telecommunications deal with Korea.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday that the United States and South Korea reached agreement on telecommunications that would provide new market opportunities for U.S. suppliers.

"The commitments undertaken by Korea through multilateral and bilateral negotiations will help ensure that U.S. telecommunications companies ... are in a position to compete in Korea's telecommunications market, which is estimated to grow to $100 billion between 1996 and 2000," Barshefsky said in a statement.

The USTR said a policy statement issued by Korea on July 14 addressed many of the concerns the United States had about its telecommunications markets. Specific policies include non-discrimination for foreign companies, non-intervention by the government in private sector procurement, more transparency in government licensing and equipment certification and increased foreign ownership in domestic service providers.

The USTR said that as a result of the policy statement and other steps by Seoul -- including joining the Information Technology Agreement to eliminate tariffs on information technology and a World Trade Organization telecommunications agreement -- the United States would remove South Korea from a special watch status under U.S. trade law that could have subjected the country to U.S. trade sanctions.
